sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. The prototype decides look and feel only (content, wording, layout, components, question order); it never decides architecture (sets, journeys, services, URL paths, field names, data-model shape, code structure). Germinal products is a sibling set of live-animals in the animals frontend. Reference lists never wait on MDM integration; address search waits on the address lookup becoming a real feature.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

sources.role: what exists today and what has already been ruled; the real persistence, validation and cross-service constraints the prototype cannot express

claims.statement: A notification is stored as one document in the MongoDB collection named "notification".
claims.quote: @org.springframework.data.mongodb.core.mapping.Document(collection = "notification")

claims.statement: The stored notification holds its identity and metadata at the top level and its content (parties, commodity, transport and so on) as a nested notification sub-object, beside a separate fulfilments payload.
claims.quote: Aggregate root: identity + metadata at the top, with the well-structured content held as a composed {@link Notification} sub-object (symmetric with the opaque {@link #fulfilments} payload).

claims.statement: Each stored notification has a string id as its database identity.
claims.quote:
@Id
    private String id;

claims.statement: A notification's reference number is unique across all notifications, and the unique index is sparse, so notifications without a reference number are allowed and do not clash with each other.
claims.quote:
@Indexed(unique = true, sparse = true)
    private String referenceNumber;

claims.statement: Each notification carries a concurrencyToken that is the record's optimistic-locking version number.
claims.quote:
@Version
    private Long concurrencyToken;

claims.statement: Each notification carries a status, one of the NotificationStatus values.
claims.quote: private NotificationStatus status;

claims.statement: Each notification records when it was created and when it was last updated, as instants (moments in time), stamped by the server.
claims.quote:
private Instant created;

    private Instant updated;

claims.statement: A client cannot set a notification's created or updated time: the request shape has no such fields and the server would discard them.
claims.quote: the aggregate's server-stamped {@code created}/{@code updated} instants are deliberately absent here; a client cannot set them and the server would discard them.

claims.statement: Each notification records submittedAt, the time of its most recent submission: set the first time it is submitted from DRAFT and refreshed whenever it is re-submitted from AMEND.
claims.quote: Timestamp of the most recent submission — set the first time the notification is submitted (from DRAFT) and refreshed whenever it is re-submitted from AMEND.

claims.statement: Starting an amendment or cancelling one leaves submittedAt unchanged, so it always points at the latest submission rather than the original one.
claims.quote: Left unchanged by amend and cancel-amend, so it always points at the latest submission event rather than the original one. Set by {@code submitNotification}; carried into the fulfilment-view projection.

claims.statement: A notification created through the app in a non-production environment carries an expiry time (expireAt), anchored to its created time, after which it becomes eligible for automatic expiry.
claims.quote: When this notification becomes eligible for automatic expiry, anchored to {@code created}. Set only for app-created notifications in non-prod environments

claims.statement: In production, and for notifications created before the expiry field existed, a notification has no expiry time.
claims.quote: {@code null} in prod and for notifications created before this field existed.

claims.statement: Expiry is driven by a sweep over a plain index rather than a database TTL index, so expiring a notification can also remove its accompanying documents.
claims.quote: Backed by a plain index (not a Mongo TTL index) so the expiry sweep can cascade to accompanying documents.

claims.statement: The expiry time is never shown in any JSON response.
Each notification stores a fulfilments payload (a list of documents recording obligation fulfilment) exactly as sent, byte for byte; the backend never interprets it.
claims.quote: Opaque obligation-fulfilment payload — persisted byte-faithfully; never interpreted by the backend.

claims.statement: When an amendment starts, the notification's content is snapshotted as it stood (including inline party details); cancelling the amendment restores that snapshot, and submitting the amendment clears it.
claims.quote: Pre-amend snapshot of {@link #notification}. Amend-only scratchpad: captured when an amendment starts, restored by cancel-amend, and cleared when the amendment is submitted. Independent of {@link #preAmendFulfilments}; carries inline party details as they stood when the trader opened the amendment.

claims.statement: The fulfilments payload is snapshotted separately when an amendment starts, restored by cancelling the amendment and cleared when it is submitted, independently of the content snapshot.
claims.quote: Pre-amend snapshot of {@link #fulfilments}. Amend-only scratchpad: restored by cancel-amend and cleared when the amendment is submitted. Independent of the content freeze.

claims.statement: Neither pre-amendment snapshot is ever shown in a JSON response.
claims.quote:
@JsonIgnore
    private Notification preAmendNotification;

claims.statement: Wherever the backend needs a notification's content, a record with no content sub-object fails at once with an error rather than carrying on; the unexpected-error handler would turn that into a 500 response.
claims.quote:
return requireNonNull(notification,
            "NotificationAggregate requires a notification sub-object at this seam");
claims.note: Inferred that the failure reaches a caller as 500: a NullPointerException is a RuntimeException, which GlobalExceptionHandler.handleException maps to 500. Which endpoints reach this seam is parts 2 and 3.

claims.statement: A request to save a notification has a body with a notification object, which is required, and an optional actor object.
A save request without a notification object is rejected with a 400 validation error naming the notification field.
claims.quote:
@NotNull
    NotificationDto notification;
claims.note: Inferred from @NotNull together with the MethodArgumentNotValidException handler. NotificationController applies @Valid to the SaveNotificationDto body at lines 52 (POST /notifications) and 71 (PUT by reference number); which endpoints those are is parts 2 and 3. The message would be the Bean Validation default ("must not be null").

claims.statement: The actor on a save request identifies who made the change: an id, a source, a user type, a display name, an organisation id and the organisation id acted on behalf of; it is passed on as the actor of the change.
claims.note: ActorRequest is not in this part's read list; it was read because SaveNotificationDto names it. Where the actor goes (the outbox Actor) is part 5.

claims.statement: The notification object in a request carries the content fields plus referenceNumber, status, concurrencyToken and the fulfilments payload.
The request shape is only ever inbound: no endpoint returns it; every endpoint returns the stored notification or one of its view projections.
claims.quote: It is never a response body — every endpoint returns {@link NotificationAggregate} or one of the view projections

claims.statement: The request shape is also the internal carrier the copy feature uses to create a new notification from an existing one.
claims.quote: Inbound request shape: the {@code notification} member of {@link SaveNotificationDto}, and the internal carrier {@link NotificationCopyMapper} hands to the create path.

claims.statement: No content field of the notification carries a validation constraint: the backend accepts any section or field missing or empty, with no required fields, lengths or formats enforced on the content.
claims.ref: src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/animals/notification/NotificationBase.java:12-50 and the section types Origin, Commodity, CommodityComplement, Species, AnimalIdentifier, Transport, Transporter, Address, ConsignmentParty, AdditionalDetails
claims.note: Inferred from absence: grep for jakarta.validation.constraints across src/main/java finds it only in SaveNotificationDto, NotificationController, DocumentUploadRequest and configuration classes; no domain type in notification/ has a constraint, so the cascading @Valid on notification has nothing to check.

claims.statement: The backend records no rule for which fields a notification must have before it can be submitted, nor any length or format rule for free-text fields such as the CPH number, email, phone or postcode.
claims.ref: src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/animals/notification/ (every domain type read in this part)
claims.note: Looked in every domain type in this slice and in GlobalExceptionHandler. Whether submit checks completeness in the service is part 2's to say.

claims.statement: The same content fields are shared by the stored content sub-object and the request shape.
claims.quote: Shared content fields extended by {@link Notification} (content sub-object) and {@link NotificationDto} (wire type).

claims.statement: A date-only field sent as a date-time, such as 2026-07-21T00:00:00Z or 2026-07-21T00:00:00, is rejected with a 400 rather than having its time part silently dropped.

A caller that sends a moment where a calendar date belongs would then be told 200, and the day it meant would depend on a zone nobody stated. With leniency off the value fails to parse and the caller gets 400.

A poller publishes waiting outbox events on a fixed delay of outbox.poller.interval-ms, 2000 ms by default.
claims.quote: @Scheduled(fixedDelayString = "${outbox.poller.interval-ms:2000}")

claims.statement: The poller is on unless outbox.poller.enabled is set to false.
claims.quote: @ConditionalOnProperty(prefix = "outbox.poller", name = "enabled", havingValue = "true", matchIfMissing = true)

claims.statement: Only one backend instance publishes at a time: each poll takes a shared lock named outbox-poller, held for at least 1 second and at most 30 seconds.
claims.quote: static final String LOCK_NAME = "outbox-poller";

claims.statement: The poller reads waiting events 10 at a time and publishes at most 500 in one run; the run limit can be set with OUTBOX_POLLER_MAX_EVENTS_PER_RUN.
claims.quote:
batch-size: 10
    max-events-per-run: ${OUTBOX_POLLER_MAX_EVENTS_PER_RUN:500}

claims.statement: A batch size or run limit of zero or less falls back to 10 and 500, and lock times left unset fall back to 1 and 30 seconds; the poll interval must be positive or the service will not start.
Events are published to one SNS topic, set by OUTBOX_SNS_TOPIC_ARN; when no topic is set, the poller publishes nothing and events stay waiting.
claims.note: OutboxConfig marks topicArn @NotBlank while application.yml defaults it to empty, so a missing value may instead stop the service from starting. The publish code is written to tolerate it.

claims.statement: The topic is an SNS FIFO topic: each message's group id is the notification's aggregateId and its deduplication id is the eventId.

.messageGroupId(event.getAggregateId())

Once an event is published it is marked with its publish time and is never published again by the poller.
A run keeps reading batches until no events are waiting, a publish fails, or the run limit is reached.

claims.statement: The service serves the list of countries at GET /countries.
claims.quote: @RequestMapping("/countries")

claims.statement: GET /countries takes one optional query parameter, blocks.
claims.quote: @RequestParam(required = false, value = "blocks") String blocks

claims.statement: GET /countries returns 200 with a JSON array of countries.
claims.quote: return ResponseEntity.ok(countries);

claims.statement: GET /countries returns countries sorted by their name.
claims.quote: .sorted(Comparator.comparing(Country::getName))

claims.statement: The country sort is a plain case-sensitive string comparison of the name, not a locale-aware collation, so names are ordered by character code.
claims.quote: Comparator.comparing(Country::getName)
claims.note: Comparator.comparing on a String uses String.compareTo; no Collator is applied.

claims.statement: The United Kingdom (effectiveAlpha2 GB) is always removed from the countries list, whatever blocks value is asked for.
claims.quote: .filter(c -> !"GB".equals(c.getEffectiveAlpha2()))

claims.statement: When blocks is given, a country is kept only if one of its MDM blocks has a name equal to the blocks value and includeCountry true.
When blocks is not given, no block filter is applied and every country except the United Kingdom is returned.
claims.quote: if (requestedBlock == null || country.getBlocks() == null) return true;

claims.statement: When blocks is given but MDM sends a country with no blocks list at all, that country is kept rather than filtered out.
claims.quote: if (requestedBlock == null || country.getBlocks() == null) return true;

claims.statement: The blocks value is also passed to MDM as its own blocks query parameter, so MDM filters first and the service filters again on includeCountry.
claims.quote: mdmClient.getCountries(ocpApimSubscriptionKey, SYSTEM, blocks);

claims.statement: The block filter compares the whole blocks value with a single block name, so asking for several blocks at once in one value (for example comma-separated) would match no country unless MDM names a block that way.
claims.quote: requestedBlock.equals(b.getName())
claims.note: No splitting of the blocks value is done anywhere in the service.

claims.statement: The block names used in tests are GBNAG_SPS_EX, GBNAG_PHYTO_EX and OMR; the service has no fixed list of allowed block values and accepts any string.
claims.quote: restTemplate.getForEntity("/countries?blocks=GBNAG_PHYTO_EX", String.class);
claims.note: No validation of the blocks parameter exists in the controller or service.

claims.statement: Each returned country has a code field, taken from MDM's effectiveAlpha2 (the ISO alpha-2 code).
claims.quote: this.code = mdmCountry.getEffectiveAlpha2();

claims.statement: Each returned country has a name field, taken from MDM's effectiveAlias (the short display name, such as "United Kingdom"), not MDM's name or longName.
claims.quote: this.name = mdmCountry.getEffectiveAlias();

claims.statement: Each returned country has a subDivisions field: a list of its subdivisions, and an empty list when MDM sends none or a null list.
claims.quote:
if (mdmSubDivisions == null || mdmSubDivisions.isEmpty()) {
      return List.of();

claims.statement: Each subdivision has a code field taken from MDM's code.value (such as ES-CN).
claims.quote: .code(subDivision.getCode().getValue())

claims.statement: Each subdivision has a name field taken from MDM's subdivision name (such as Canary Islands).
claims.quote: .name(subDivision.getName())

claims.statement: A subdivision MDM sends with no code, or a code with no value, is dropped from the country's subdivisions.
claims.quote:
.filter(subDivision -> subDivision.getCode() != null
            && subDivision.getCode().getValue() != null)

claims.statement: Subdivisions are returned in the order MDM sends them; they are not sorted.
claims.quote: return mdmSubDivisions.stream()
claims.note: No sort is applied in mapSubDivisions or anywhere else to subdivisions.

claims.statement: A country is returned with only code, name and subDivisions: MDM's longName, name, independent, statusName, system, systemAlias, systemAlpha2, systemAlpha3, systemLongName, effectiveAlpha3, effectiveLongName and blocks are all dropped.
An MDM subdivision's blocs list is dropped; a subdivision is returned with only code and name.
claims.quote: private List<String> blocs;

A subdivision code arrives from MDM wrapped in an object with a single value field.

claims.statement: The stub simulates the DEFRA address lookup gateway's address search at GET /simulator/address-lookup/v2.1/addresses.
claims.quote: @GetMapping("/simulator/address-lookup/v2.1/addresses")

claims.statement: The simulator stands in for the address lookup gateway that the INS backend calls, as part of the EUDPA-390 address lookup spike.
claims.quote: # EUDPA-390 address lookup spike — the three federated-credential simulators (plan Step 6).
claims.note: The caller being ins-backend is stated in the application.yml comment at line 115: "The audience ins-backend's Entra token request resolves to".

claims.statement: The search accepts two optional query parameters: postcode and find (free text).
claims.quote:
@RequestParam(required = false) String postcode,
        @RequestParam(required = false) String find

claims.statement: When both postcode and find are sent, postcode is used and find is ignored.
claims.quote: String term = postcode != null ? postcode : find;

claims.statement: A postcode and a find term are matched the same way, against the same reserved terms: the simulator deliberately does not model what find really matches (a postcode, building name or number, street or town), leaving that to the real gateway in dev.
claims.quote: Deliberately identical for both parameters. What find really matches — a postcode, a building name or number, a street, a town — is a question only the real gateway can answer, and a simulator that guessed would look like an answer. Local runs prove the plumbing carries the parameter through; dev settles the behaviour.

claims.statement: When neither postcode nor find is sent, the simulator answers 400 with a JSON body whose message is "Either postcode or find is required".
claims.quote: .body("{ \"statusCode\": 400, \"message\": \"Either postcode or find is required\" }");

claims.statement: Reserved terms are matched exactly, case and spacing included, so a postcode sent in lower case or without its space (for example sw1a 1aa or SW1A1AA) does not hit a fixture and gets the no-results answer.
claims.quote:
return switch (term) {
            case "SW1A 1AA" -> jsonOk(THREE_ADDRESSES_FIXTURE);
claims.note: Inferred from the Java string switch, which compares exactly, and the default branch returning NO_RESULTS_FIXTURE. Whether callers normalise the postcode before sending it is outside this source.

claims.statement: Searching for postcode SW1A 1AA returns 200 with a JSON body holding the three fixture addresses.
claims.quote: case "SW1A 1AA" -> jsonOk(THREE_ADDRESSES_FIXTURE);

claims.statement: Searching for postcode ZZ1 1ZZ returns 204 No Content with no body: the reserved no-results postcode.
claims.quote: case "ZZ1 1ZZ" -> ResponseEntity.noContent().build();

claims.statement: Searching for postcode QQ1 1QQ returns 400 with a JSON body whose message is "Requested postcode is not valid": the reserved invalid postcode.
claims.quote: .body("{\"statusCode\":400,\"message\":\"Requested postcode is not valid\"}");

claims.statement: Searching for postcode XX1 1XX returns 503 with a JSON body whose message is "Service Unavailable": the reserved throttled or unavailable postcode.
claims.quote: .body("{\"statusCode\":503,\"message\":\"Service Unavailable\"}");

claims.statement: Searching for postcode YY1 1YY returns 200 with an HTML body ("Bad Gateway") instead of JSON: the reserved proxy-error postcode.
claims.quote: case "YY1 1YY" -> ResponseEntity.ok().contentType(MediaType.TEXT_HTML).body("<html><body>Bad Gateway</body></html>");

claims.statement: Searching for postcode TT1 1TT waits 15 seconds, then returns 200 with the three fixture addresses: the reserved slow-response postcode.
claims.quote: Thread.sleep(15_000);

claims.statement: The free-text terms "Buckingham Palace" and "Downing Street" each return 200 with the three fixture addresses, so the find search can be demonstrated locally.
claims.quote: case "Buckingham Palace", "Downing Street" -> jsonOk(THREE_ADDRESSES_FIXTURE);

claims.statement: A result for a reserved free-text term says nothing about whether the same search would return results from the real gateway: the free-text terms are fixtures, not a model of find.
claims.quote: These are reserved terms like the postcodes above, NOT a model of what find matches — that is the question the spike exists to answer, and only the real gateway can. A search here returning results says nothing about whether the same search would return results in dev.

claims.statement: Every other postcode or free-text term returns 200 with a JSON body holding no results: header totalResults "0" and an empty results list.
claims.quote: { "header": { "totalResults": "0" }, "results": [] }

claims.quote:
"header": { "totalResults": "3" },

claims.statement: The fixtures follow the real gateway's dev response of 17 September 2026, not the published v2.1 specification.
claims.quote: Shaped like the real dev response of 2026-09-17, not like the published v2.1 specification

claims.statement: The three fixture addresses are the three ways a name lands in a result (the whole name in subBuildingName; a building number and street; a sub-building, building name and street), chosen because they make composing address line 1 awkward; the Buckingham Palace case is the one dev actually returned.
claims.quote: The three results are the three ways a name lands, which is what makes composing address line 1 awkward — the first is the Buckingham Palace case dev actually returned, where {@code subBuildingName} carries the whole name and {@code buildingName}, {@code buildingNumber} and {@code street} are all null.

claims.statement: Every search requires a bearer token: the simulator checks the authorisation scheme, the token's signature, its audience and its expiry before answering any search, the way a real resource server would.
claims.quote: Checks the bearer token the way a real resource server would — signature, audience, expiry — before serving the reserved-postcode fixtures
claims.note: Described in general terms only, as the brief requires.

claims.statement: A search with a missing or invalid bearer token is refused with 401 and the JSON body { "statusCode": 401, "message": "Unauthorized. Access token is missing or invalid." }, word for word what the real gateway returned in dev on 17 September 2026.
claims.quote: .body("{ \"statusCode\": 401, \"message\": \"Unauthorized. Access token is missing or invalid.\" }");

claims.statement: The 401 answer carries no WWW-Authenticate header, matching the real gateway.
claims.quote: The gateway sends no {@code WWW-Authenticate} header with it, and neither does this.

claims.statement: The bearer check runs before the search terms are looked at, so an unauthorised request gets 401 even when it sends no search term or a reserved term.

The audience the simulator expects is set by address-lookup-simulator.expected-audience, overridable with ADDRESS_LOOKUP_SIMULATOR_EXPECTED_AUDIENCE, and must match the INS backend's local and stack Scope value exactly, api:// prefix included.
claims.quote:
# The audience ins-backend's Entra token request resolves to once /.default is stripped — must
  # match the local/stack "Scope" value in the EUDPA-390 plan exactly, api:// prefix included.
claims.note: The default value is a placeholder identifier, not a secret, and is not repeated here.

claims.statement: The simulator, like the real gateway in dev, accepts only the api:// form of the audience and refuses a token whose audience is the bare identifier.
claims.quote:
# The real gateway policy in dev wants the api:// form and rejects the bare GUID, so this does
  # too: a simulator that accepted either would not have caught the 401 the spike hit.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint requires an Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key request header; Spring rejects a request without it, so a call with no key is refused (a bad request) rather than answered.
claims.note: The header is required by default (@RequestHeader with no required=false). The 400 outcome is Spring's default for a missing required header, not code in the stub.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint takes an optional blocks query parameter but does not filter on it: every call returns the whole fixture, whichever block is asked for or if none is.

Outside this slice, trade-imports-reference-data's MdmService passes system GBNAG and blocks to MDM and then filters the answer by block itself (isIncludedInRequestedBlock), so on the stack the filtering a user sees is done by reference-data, not by the stub.

A country's block membership is a record of the block name, an includeCountry boolean and a list of string tags.
A subdivision record carries a code (an object holding a single value string), a name and a list of blocs (spelt blocs, not blocks).

claims.statement: The stub's latency configuration names the MDM integration as "MDM reference data through APIM: countries and border control posts", owned by the MDM / data platform team, covering the two paths /mdm/geo/countries and /mdm/trade/bcp/poes.

mdm:
      interface-name: "MDM reference data through APIM: countries and border control posts"
      owner: MDM / data platform team

claims.statement: By default the MDM paths answer with no added delay (profile zero-delay), and the interim service-level targets are p50 100 ms, p95 400 ms and p99 1,000 ms, recorded as not agreed.
claims.note: The latency profiles themselves are out of scope; this claim records only what the block says for the two MDM paths.

claims.statement: The README says the stub stands in for MDM reference data through APIM, which trade-imports-reference-data calls, on GET /mdm/geo/countries and GET /mdm/trade/bcp/poes.

claims.quote: | `mdm` | `GET /mdm/geo/countries`, `GET /mdm/trade/bcp/poes` |
claims.note: The fault kinds and controls are out of scope.

claims.statement: The stub has no block other than GBNAG_SPS_EX and ignores the blocks parameter, so it cannot offer a germinal-products country list, or any list that differs between the live-animals and germinal-products journeys, on the local stack.
claims.note: Looked for any other block name in the fixture with jq and for any blocks handling in the controller; there is none. Whether germinal products need a different block is for the requirement sources to say.

claims.statement: The countries fixture offers no country outside the EU and EFTA, so a live-animals or germinal-products notification from a non-European country of origin cannot be made against the stub.
claims.note: Looked at all 31 country records. Whether the journeys need non-European origins is for the requirement sources to say.

claims.statement: Port records carry no type or transport mode (airport, seaport, road, rail), so the stub cannot narrow ports by how the consignment arrives.
claims.note: Looked at the record and all 78 fixture entries: only id, code and name. A type can only be guessed from the name.

claims.statement: Port records say nothing about which commodities a border control post is designated for (such as live animals or germinal products), so the stub cannot offer different port lists to the live-animals and germinal-products journeys.
claims.note: Looked at the record, all 78 fixture entries and the controller's parameters; there is no designation field and no filter parameter.

claims.statement: Subdivisions carry no region or block data in the fixture, so the stub cannot show whether a region such as the Canary Islands or Madeira is treated differently from its country for live animals or germinal products.
claims.note: Looked at all nine subdivision entries; none sets blocs. Whether the journeys need region-level origin is for the requirement sources to say.

claims.statement: When the simulator refuses a bearer because its audience does not match, it logs a warning naming the audience the token carried, so a developer can see from the stub's log which audience was sent. The other refusals (no bearer, bad signature, expiry) are not logged.
claims.quote: log.warn("Address lookup simulator rejected a bearer with audience {}", claims.getAudience());

claims.statement: The simulator has two different no-results answers: the reserved postcode ZZ1 1ZZ gives 204 with no body, while any unreserved term gives 200 with totalResults "0" and an empty results list, so a caller exercised against the stub meets both shapes.

claims.statement: The fixture gives Reunion the subdivision code FR-LRE and spells the name without its accent; FR-LRE is not the ISO 3166-2 form the other French codes follow (two letters after FR-, such as FR-MQ or FR-GP), so a page or mapping keyed on ISO subdivision codes would not match Reunion from the stub.
claims.note: Inferred from the pattern of the five other French subdivision codes in the same list; whether live MDM also uses FR-LRE is not knowable from the stub.

claims.statement: The ports fixture holds no Northern Ireland port (such as Belfast or Larne): all 78 entries are Great Britain ports, so a journey that needs a Northern Ireland point of entry cannot be exercised against the stub.
claims.note: Looked at every name and code in the fixture; none is in Northern Ireland.

claims.statement: The live-animals notification model is the Live Animals V4 data-field model, taken from the Confluence page "Live Animals Data Fields - V4" (page 6497338582).

* Obligations — Live Animals V4 data-field model.
 *
 * Source: Confluence "Live Animals Data Fields - V4" (page 6497338582).

claims.statement: The notification manifest declares 49 obligations, and the order they are listed in does not affect evaluation.
claims.quote:
// Manifest — order does not affect evaluation (evaluator builds group
// hierarchy via `within` back-references).
claims.note: 49 is counted from the obligations array, lines 183-231.

claims.statement: A notification holds three repeatable groups: commodity lines, animal-identifier records within each line, and accompanying documents. Groups are derived from the obligations that point at them with `within`.
claims.note: The three groups follow from the within references in lines.js (commodityLine), identifiers.js (unitRecord) and documents.js (documents).

claims.statement: No notification-level all-or-nothing invariant across scalar fields exists today.
Option lists for commodities, species, ports of entry, country of origin and animals-certified-for come from MDM in production and are stubbed in test fixtures; they are not modelled as obligations.
claims.quote:
* MDM-sourced enum values (commodities / species / ports of
 * entry / country of origin / animals-certified-for options) are
 * stubbed in test fixtures rather than modelled as obligations —
 * their real option lists come from MDM in production.

claims.statement: A standard address block is a single answer whose stored value is a composite of name, address line 1, optional address line 2, town, optional county, postcode, country, telephone and email.
claims.quote:
* Standard address block: modelled as a single-cardinality obligation
 * whose stored value is a composite `{ name, addressLine1,
 * addressLine2?, town, county?, postCode, country, telephone, email }`.

claims.statement: Validation of an address block's subfields (maximum lengths, formats, which subfields are mandatory) is outside the obligation model.
claims.quote:
* Field-level validation of the composite (max-length, formats,
 * mandatory subfields) is out of scope of the obligation model.

claims.statement: The model does not say anywhere which address subfields are mandatory or what limits they carry; that rule must live in the address pages or the address book, outside this slice.
claims.note: Looked in parties.js, misc.js, transport.js and the manifest header. Only the composite shape is stated.

XXXXXX is a 6-char Crockford base32

The documents feature also caps the Add affordance at 15 and enforces the cap on its write path.
claims.quote:
The document collection has a maximum of fifteen entries. The set manifest declares
the cardinality and the documents feature enforces it on its write path.

sources.role: how the real services behave end to end today

claims.statement: An unauthenticated user who opens the animals notification dashboard (/live-animals) is redirected to the frontend's sign-in route, which carries the requested path as a redirect parameter.
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3000/live-animals -> /auth/sign-in?redirect=%2Flive-animals

claims.statement: The frontend's sign-in route redirects the browser to the Defra ID authorise endpoint (the stub on localhost:3007) for the b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi policy.
claims.quote: http://localhost:3007/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi/oauth2/v2.0/authorize?serviceId=trade-imports-animals-frontend&p=b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi&response_mode=query&client_id=test-client-id&response_type=code&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A3000%2Fauth%2Fsign-in-oidc&state=[REDACTED]&scope=openid%20offline_access%20test-client-id
claims.note: The state value differs per run; redacted here as a per-session value.

claims.statement: The authorise request is an OpenID Connect authorisation-code request: response_type code, response_mode query, scope openid offline_access plus the client id, and redirect_uri pointing at the frontend's /auth/sign-in-oidc callback.
claims.quote: response_mode=query&client_id=test-client-id&response_type=code&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A3000%2Fauth%2Fsign-in-oidc

claims.statement: The authorise request names the calling service with a serviceId parameter of trade-imports-animals-frontend.
claims.quote: serviceId=trade-imports-animals-frontend

claims.statement: The Defra ID stub's authorise endpoint redirects to its own sign-in page at /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp.
claims.quote: GET 302 ... /oauth2/v2.0/authorize?... -> /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp

claims.statement: Opening the notification dashboard while signed out lands the user on the sign-in page, whose main heading is 'Sign in using Government Gateway'.
claims.quote: Sign in using Government Gateway

claims.statement: The sign-in page's browser title is 'Trade Imports Defra ID stub - GOV.UK'.
claims.quote: Trade Imports Defra ID stub - GOV.UK

claims.statement: The sign-in page's service navigation names the service 'Trade Imports Defra ID stub', and that service-name section is rendered twice, one under the other.
claims.ref: trace be93a action call@263 header section.govuk-service-navigation (two copies)
claims.quote: Trade Imports Defra ID stub
claims.note: The duplicate service navigation section is a rendering defect in the stub, not in the animals frontend.

claims.statement: The sign-in page carries a phase banner tagged 'Basic' with no banner text.
claims.quote: Basic

claims.statement: The sign-in page asks for a Government Gateway user ID in a text input (name crn).
claims.ref: trace be93a action call@263 label[for=crn], input#crn
claims.quote: Government Gateway user ID

claims.statement: The user ID field has the hint 'This could be up to 12 characters.'
claims.quote: This could be up to 12 characters.
claims.note: The hint says up to 12 characters while the error message asks for a 10-digit customer reference number (CRN); recorded, not reconciled.

claims.statement: The sign-in page asks for a password in a password-type input (name password).
claims.ref: trace be93a action call@263 label[for=password], input#password type=password
claims.quote: Password

claims.statement: The sign-in form submits with a button labelled 'Sign in'.
claims.quote: Sign in

claims.statement: The sign-in form posts the user ID and password as form-encoded fields crn and password to the stub's /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp.
claims.quote: <FORM method="POST" action="/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp"> ... crn=2100010101&password=[REDACTED]

claims.statement: Below the form, the sign-in page shows a link 'I have forgotten my password'; its href is '#', so it goes nowhere.

claims.statement: The sign-in page has a Details component with the summary 'Help signing in'.
claims.ref: trace be93a action call@263 details.govuk-details summary

claims.statement: Signing in with a user ID that is not a valid customer reference number keeps the user on the sign-in page, and the stub answers the post with HTTP 400.
claims.quote: POST 400 http://localhost:3007/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp crn=invalid&password=[REDACTED]

claims.statement: After a bad user ID, the sign-in page shows an error summary titled 'There is a problem' with the message 'Enter a valid 10-digit customer reference number (CRN) and password'.
claims.quote: There is a problem ... Error: Enter a valid 10-digit customer reference number (CRN) and password

claims.statement: Signing in with a valid user ID but a wrong password also keeps the user on the sign-in page with HTTP 400.
claims.quote: POST 400 http://localhost:3007/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp crn=2100010101&password=[REDACTED]

claims.statement: After a wrong password, the sign-in page shows the same error summary and message as for a bad user ID, so the user is not told which of the two was wrong.
claims.quote: There is a problem ... Error: Enter a valid 10-digit customer reference number (CRN) and password

claims.statement: After a failed sign-in, the user ID field keeps the value entered and the password field is empty.
claims.ref: trace 8c7b9 action call@303 input#crn, input#password; trace 57464 action call@237
claims.quote: <INPUT ... id="crn" name="crn" type="text" value="invalid" ...> <INPUT ... id="password" name="password" type="password">

claims.statement: The sign-in error summary departs from the GOV.UK Error summary pattern: the message is a span inside the list rather than a list item linking to the field, and neither input is marked with a field-level error message or error class.
claims.quote: Error: Enter a valid 10-digit customer reference number (CRN) and password
claims.note: The standard component would replace this with an li containing an anchor to #crn, plus govuk-form-group--error and an inline error message on the field. This is the stub's page, not the animals frontend's.

claims.statement: A correct user ID and password make the stub redirect to its /organisations step, which immediately redirects back to the frontend's /auth/sign-in-oidc callback with an authorisation code and the original state; no organisation choice is shown.
claims.quote: POST 302 .../oauth2/authresp -> /organisations; GET 302 http://localhost:3007/organisations -> http://localhost:3000/auth/sign-in-oidc?code=[REDACTED]&state=[REDACTED]

claims.statement: The frontend's /auth/sign-in-oidc callback redirects the signed-in user to the path held in the original redirect parameter (here the dashboard /live-animals).
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3000/auth/sign-in-oidc?code=[REDACTED]&state=[REDACTED] -> /live-animals

claims.statement: Signing in from the dashboard lands the user on the notification dashboard at /live-animals, whose main heading is 'Import notification service'.
claims.quote: Import notification service

claims.statement: On sign-in the frontend sets a session cookie that lasts 4 hours (Max-Age 14400), HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax.
claims.quote: session=[REDACTED]; Max-Age=14400; Expires=Wed, 07 Oct 2026 21:40:15 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/

claims.statement: On sign-in the frontend also sets sid and crumb cookies, both HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, and clears the temporary bell-defra-id cookie.
claims.quote: bell-defra-id=[REDACTED]; Max-Age=0; ... crumb=[REDACTED]; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/ ... sid=[REDACTED]; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/
claims.note: None of the cookies carries the Secure flag on the local http stack.

claims.statement: The dashboard's browser title repeats the service name: 'Import notification service - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
claims.quote: Import notification service - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: Once signed in, the service navigation names the service 'Import notification service', linking to /live-animals.
claims.quote: Import notification service

claims.statement: Once signed in, the service navigation has four items in order: Dashboard, Address book, Manage account, Log out.
claims.quote: Dashboard / Address book / Manage account / Log out

claims.statement: On the dashboard the Dashboard navigation item is marked active (aria-current) and links to /live-animals.
claims.quote: Dashboard

claims.quote: Address book

claims.statement: The Manage account navigation item has href '#', so it goes nowhere yet.
claims.quote: Manage account

claims.statement: The sign-out control is a service navigation link labelled 'Log out' that points at /auth/sign-out.
claims.quote: Log out

claims.statement: The signed-in header shows no signed-in identity: no email address, name or 'signed in as' strip appears in the header or navigation.
claims.ref: trace 0b934 action call@259 header; trace 27de2 action call@262 (auth.spec.ts:57)
claims.quote: expect(getByText('test.user11@defra.gov.uk')).toHaveCount(0)
claims.note: In trace 27de2 the count-0 assertion finished (17555.6 ms) about 2 ms before the dashboard document finished loading (17557.9 ms), and its last DOM snapshot is still the stub sign-in page, so that trace alone does not prove the absence. The absence is confirmed from the dashboard header rendered in trace 0b934 call@259, which carries no user identity.

claims.quote: sid=[REDACTED]; Max-Age=0; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/

claims.statement: After Log out the user lands on the Defra ID stub's page with the heading 'You have signed out'.
claims.quote: You have signed out

claims.ref: trace 68f5b action call@295, call@299; request GET /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-TBYAW8/origin (auth.spec.ts:87)

claims.statement: The unauthenticated deep-link tests start from no session at all: the test keeps only cookies whose names start 'liveAnimals', and the browser held none (its cookies were trade-imports-defra-id-stub-session, crumb, sid and session), so every cookie was cleared before the deep link.
claims.ref: trace 68f5b action call@289 (cookies result), call@293 (addCookies with an empty list); trace d79c5 action call@283, call@287
claims.quote: const journeyCookies = (await pages.page.context().cookies()).filter(({ name }) => name.startsWith('liveAnimals'));
claims.note: Inferred from the cookie names the trace recorded and the empty addCookies call: the journey state is held server-side against the notification reference, not in a liveAnimals cookie.

claims.statement: The animals frontend sends a Content-Security-Policy header on the dashboard document response.
claims.quote: Content-Security-Policy: base-uri 'self';connect-src 'self' wss data:;default-src 'self';font-src 'self' data:;form-action 'self' http://localhost:3002;frame-ancestors 'none';frame-src 'self' data:;img-src 'self' data:;manifest-src 'self';media-src 'self';object-src 'none';script-src 'self' 'sha256-GUQ5ad8JK5KmEWmROf3LZd9ge94daqNvd8xy9YS1iDw=';style-src 'self';worker-src 'self'

claims.statement: The CSP restricts scripts to the frontend's own origin plus one inline script allowed by its SHA-256 hash.
claims.quote: script-src 'self' 'sha256-GUQ5ad8JK5KmEWmROf3LZd9ge94daqNvd8xy9YS1iDw='

claims.statement: The CSP lets forms post to the frontend itself and to the address book service's origin (localhost:3002).
claims.quote: form-action 'self' http://localhost:3002

claims.statement: The CSP forbids framing the frontend and forbids plugins and object embeds.
claims.quote: frame-ancestors 'none'; ... object-src 'none'

claims.statement: The CSP limits styles, fonts, images, media, manifests and workers to the frontend's own origin, with data: URIs also allowed for fonts, images, frames and connections.
claims.quote: connect-src 'self' wss data:;default-src 'self';font-src 'self' data:;frame-src 'self' data:;img-src 'self' data:;manifest-src 'self';media-src 'self';style-src 'self';worker-src 'self'

claims.statement: The CSP header is also present on the frontend's redirect responses (/live-animals 302 and /auth/sign-in 302) and on the /auth/sign-in-oidc callback, not only on rendered pages.
claims.quote: Content-Security-Policy

claims.statement: The dashboard response also sends Strict-Transport-Security for one year including subdomains.
claims.quote: strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains

claims.statement: The dashboard response sends X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Download-Options noopen and X-XSS-Protection '1; mode=block'.
claims.quote: x-frame-options: DENY; x-content-type-options: nosniff; x-download-options: noopen; x-xss-protection: 1; mode=block

claims.statement: The dashboard response is sent with Cache-Control no-cache.
claims.quote: cache-control: no-cache

claims.statement: The corpus never submits the sign-in form with an empty user ID or an empty password, so the message for missing credentials is not recorded.
claims.ref: auth.spec.ts (only 'invalid' user id and 'invalid' password cases); traces 8c7b9, 57464

claims.statement: No trace exercises session expiry: what a user sees when the 4-hour session cookie lapses, or whether a timeout warning is shown, is not recorded.
No trace follows the post-logout callback /auth/sign-out-oidc, so what the frontend does there (clearing the remaining session cookie, where it redirects) is not recorded.
The stub's /organisations step redirects straight back without showing a page, so the corpus never shows an organisation or business choice for a user linked to more than one organisation.
The service root / is only opened while signed in; whether an unauthenticated visit to / redirects to the default set first or straight to sign-in is not recorded.
The CSP and security headers are only recorded for the animals frontend; the Defra ID stub's sign-in and signed-out pages were not checked for them by any test.

claims.statement: Copying does not change the source notification, so a second copy can reuse the same concurrency token.

sources.role: policy for the germinal products set: which data a germinal products notification captures, each field's format, whether it is mandatory or optional and where it applies. Governs data, not look and feel: the prototype still decides how pages look and read.

claims.statement: The Germinal Data Elements section defines data elements that apply to germinal products only.
claims.quote: This section defines the data elements that apply to germinal products only

claims.statement: Germinal products are semen, embryos and ova.
claims.quote: semen, embryos and ova

claims.statement: A germinal products notification must be submitted with at least one germinal identifier per animal.
claims.quote: A notification must be submitted with at least one germinal identifier per animal
claims.note: Ambiguous: germinal products are not animals, and every Unit Level field in the table below is marked Optional. See the gap claim that follows.

claims.statement: The page does not say which fields count as a 'germinal identifier' for the at-least-one rule, what 'per animal' means for semen, embryos and ova (per commodity line, per unit or per donor), or at which point the rule is enforced (to proceed or at submit). All four Unit Level identifier fields (Donor name/ID, Collection date, Production date, Identification Number/Mark) are marked Optional, which on its own would let a notification be submitted with none.
claims.ref: §Germinal Data Elements, intro paragraph against the field table's Mandatory column

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: Obligation commodityType: the notification's commodity type is mandatory.
Obligation commodityLines: a notification must hold at least one commodity line, with the error code obligation.commodityLines.atLeastOne; it is a structural group, always in scope.
Obligation category: every commodity line must have a category, and it is the gate every other per-line field reads.
Obligation quantity: every commodity line must have a quantity, whatever its category, so it has no gate.

claims.statement: Obligation genus: mandatory on lines whose category asks for a genus (plants for planting, trees for planting and both hardwood categories), and out of scope otherwise.
Obligation species: mandatory on plants for planting and trees for planting lines only.
Obligation commodityCode: mandatory on every plants and wood category line, and not on potato lines.
Obligation potatoVariety: mandatory on seed and ware potato lines only.
Obligation potatoIntendedUse: mandatory on seed and ware potato lines only.
Obligation eppoCode: mandatory on plants for planting and trees for planting lines only.
Obligation sizeOfTree: mandatory on trees for planting and cut coniferous trees lines only.
Obligation phytosanitaryTreatments: mandatory on the five wood category lines only.

Each category-gated per-line obligation explains its applicability with the code obligation.{field}.applicable.becauseCategory ('{field} applies on lines whose category asks for it'), and reads its category list lazily when the gate runs.

code: `obligation.${field}.applicable.becauseCategory`,

claims.statement: There is no commodity catalogue or commodity search: commodity code is free text checked only for presence and length, with no lookup against the UK Trade Tariff or MDM. Looked in services/commodities/index.js, line-form.js and details.controller.js.

claims.statement: Each address-book picker row shows the address as one line made of address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county and postal or zip code, in that order, joined with commas, skipping empty parts and leaving the country out because it has its own column.
claims.quote:
const ADDRESS_PARTS = [
  'addressLine1',
  'addressLine2',
  'townOrCity',
  'county',
  'postalOrZipCode'
]

/** The address as one line for the results table. The country has its own
 * column, so it is left out here. */
export const addressText = (address = {}) =>
  ADDRESS_PARTS.map((part) => address[part])
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join(', ')

A picker selection counts only if the address book still holds that record: a missing or soft-deleted id is treated as no selection, the same as a stored reference to a deleted record reading as never entered.

claims.statement: A page number in the place of destination link or form that is not a number is read as the first page.

claims.note: The page number travels as a hidden 'page' field in the form (template.njk:21). A new search, by contrast, always goes back to page one (p7-055).

claims.statement: If the address book record a saved contact was copied from is later deleted, the consignment contact page shows no 'Selected address' inset and no ticked row for it, and does not carry it in the paging links, although the copied contact stays saved on the notification.
claims.note: Inferred by combining two facts: GET selects the saved answer's addressId (controller.js:73), which renderPicker resolves through chosenFor and drops when the record is missing or deleted; and the contact answer is a copy that the read-path sanitiser never clears (parties/index.js:15-19). So the page and the stored answer disagree once the source record is deleted. No fit spec covers this case.

claims.statement: A consignment contact whose address-book record has since been deleted shows 'Not provided' on the Contact card with no error and nothing blocking Continue, because the contact is not one of the reference parties that get a correction error (only place of destination and consignor do).
claims.quote:
export const REFERENCE_PARTIES = Object.freeze([
  PLACE_OF_DESTINATION,
  CONSIGNOR
])
claims.note: partiesFor resolves contactAddress by its addressId and drops it when deleted, so the card rows fall back to Not provided; outstandingPartyErrors only iterates REFERENCE_PARTIES. parties/index.js says the contact answer holds a copy of the address, yet check answers still displays it from the book, not from the stored copy.

claims.statement: Check answers works out its party errors from the stored answers rather than the sanitised ones, because the sanitiser drops the unresolved references the page must name; the rest of the page uses the sanitised answers.

claims.statement: d-026 dissent: the trees-for-planting hint must not name Annex 1's first-group genera as 'trees'. That would put a policy classification nobody made into notifier-facing copy, so the hint stays neutral and lets the trader self-classify. A hint is still required, because a self-classification radio needs one the trader can act on.
claims.quote: Policy judge wanted the trees-for-planting hint to name Annex 1's first-group genera as the trees ('sweet chestnut, cedar, ash, olive, spruce, pine, plane, plum or cherry, oak or elm') — lost because Annex 1 never labels that group 'trees', Olea and Prunus sit in it awkwardly, and naming them would put a policy classification nobody made into notifier-facing copy; the neutral self-classification hint is used instead. Engine judge proposed no hint at all — lost because a self-classification radio needs a hint the trader can act on
